The question as to whether they would "like it or not" given their situation may feel awkward to respond to. There could be more clarification around what exactly that means in their current situation (I know some upfront effort was there). 

For example, is it getting at that potentially sharing X dish may spoil their enjoyment of it (and interpreting that within their intimacy level)?

Good study. Thank you for the work!

This was really hard to wrap my head around, especially the choice before the actions. The instructions said, "By how much the two people would like the food, we mean how much eating it would satisfy the motivational state they are in right now — for example, how hungry they are, or how much they like or are interested in that kind of food. This is about the appeal of the food itself, separate from what they decide to do and from how easy or hard it is to get or eat the food." Well, if we don't know about each person's preference, how can we determine how much they like the food with no background information? Just seems flawed to me.
The instructions were a little difficult but once I started I understood better. An example would be nice.
It was hard deciding how much BOTH liked the food when it boiled down to one eating it and the other not, but I guess that's part of the survey! I wonder what's the point of this...?
I did my best with the memory checks, I wasn't as focused on the names of the individuals as I was the details of each interaction, their relationship to one another, etc.

I apologize if I got the names wrong on the memory recall, there were a lot of scenarios with different names, and the names didn't seem as important as the scenarios so I didn't think to remember them.

I might have got that last question wrong, I answered every question in the moment exactly how I felt and read it properly, I just kind of forgot the very specific details, I was more focused on the food than names or places.
